title: Registry seeding & operator bundle design proposal
content:
Objective:
Produce an operationally simple, secure, and repeatable approach to seed an offline/air-gapped customer registry with operator bundles, container images, model artifacts and dependency bundles. The goal is a general-purpose registry seeding workflow + a Terraform module interface for installing the operator and bootstrapping the runtime in VPC/on-prem environments.

Why this differs from other drafts:
- Focus is on an idempotent seeding workflow (able to resume across interrupted transfer windows).
- Includes delta-friendly bundle layout to support incremental upgrades with minimal bandwidth.
- Strong emphasis on verification: SBOMs, cosign signatures, and content-addressed checksums tied to Terraform inputs for auditable installs.

Constraints / assumptions:
- Target clusters are air-gapped (no outbound internet) but have a controlled transfer mechanism (sneakernet, secure bastion transfer, or customer-provided proxy).
- Customers may have strict FIPS/KMS requirements; all signing and encryption should be optional via flags.
- Typical seed window 4–48 hours depending on customer bandwidth; default design assumes limited bandwidth ~200 Mbps sustained.
- Both OCI images (operators, sidecars) and large model artifact blobs (S3-style objects) must be supported.

High-level design (three phases):
1) Bundle composition (build-time)
   - Produce a seed bundle archive for each release stream (stable, canary, rollbackable). Each bundle contains:
     * registry-manifest.json (list of all OCI refs + layers, size, sha256)
     * operator-bundles/ (catalog-operator bundles, CSVs, package manifests)
     * images/ (OCI tarballs or repository layout)
     * models/ (sharded model blobs, optional dedup index)
     * sboms/ (CycloneDX v1.4 for images and artifacts)
     * signatures/ (cosign signatures for images and archive, optional)
